chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Barqī, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Khazzāz, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said:

I was present with Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), and a man said to him, “May Allah keep you well. You mentioned that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (عليه السلام) used to wear coarse clothing, and used to wear a shirt for four dirhams and the like of that, while we see new clothing upon you.”

So he said to him, “Indeed, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (عليه السلام) used to wear that in a time when it was not objected to in his case. If he were to wear something like that today, he would become known by it. So the best clothing of every age is the clothing of its people, except that our Qāʾim from the Ahl al-Bayt (عليه السلام), when he rises, will wear the garments of ʿAlī (عليه السلام) and proceed according to the conduct of ʿAlī (عليه السلام).”

key_terms.بِسِيرَةِ عَلِيٍّ: according to the conduct and way of ʿAlī (عليه السلام)
key_terms.ثِيَابَ عَلِيٍّ: the garments of ʿAlī (عليه السلام), indicating his mode and style
key_terms.شُهِرَ بِهِ: he would become conspicuous or publicly marked by it
key_terms.قَائِمَنَا: our Qāʾim, the one who will rise from the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.لِبَاسُ أَهْلِهِ: the customary clothing of the people of that time

ai.seo_question: Why did Imām al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام) wear newer clothes if Imām ʿAlī (عليه السلام) wore coarse garments?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that outward practices such as clothing may vary according to time and social custom, and that appropriateness is judged within the context of one’s age. It also affirms that the Qāʾim from the Ahl al-Bayt (عليه السلام) will revive the way and conduct of Imām ʿAlī (عليه السلام).
